reply.rationale: No proposed segmentation meets the paradigm-evidence threshold. Many apparent similarities are just shared substrings across unrelated whole-code meanings (e.g. hot-/ho-, slide-, wobble-, tone/TONE, CO-, -bright, -ROTATE). The abbreviation set (de, hd, hl, tb, p2, bb, fl, ss, wb, ob, fr, cl, le, hc) is best treated as opaque aliases for whole stored instructions, not productive morphology. The digit cases also fail securely as morphology here: although COOL-FAN-2 and COOL-FAN-6 differ semantically, the dataset does not support a broader compositional network with stable substituting morphemes beyond these isolated labels, and the codebook is rich in synonymous whole-code renamings, so false segmentation is a higher risk than flat storage. Because no defensible multi-entry paradigm with stable substitution classes and predictable whole meanings survives all tests, the safest complete partition is a flat lexicon.
